top_choice_rationale: P001 gives a mature, independently reproduced achievement (the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock reaching ~1e-18) with an allocation, Katori and Ye, that every member converged on and that a narrow citation can bound without reaching into the comb and ion-trap prizes. I still regard it as a refinement of measurement capability more than a new window on nature, but its reach into precision tests of fundamental physics makes it defensible. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a genuine prediction-then-observation story, but its allocation is contested (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan, 2D versus 3D) and it sits close to the 2016 prize, so it ranks second. Awarding nothing is the weakest option, since a mature, well-supported candidate is available.
